title: Towards Robust Low-Spatial-Frequency Imaging with Ptychographic Holography
content: Phase retrieval imaging, or solving the “phase problem,” entails determining the full complex specimen wavefunction despite only measuring real-valued intensities. Zernike phase contrast in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) [1] and iterative ptychography in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) are the current leading such techniques in either modality [2]. These methods can improve studies of low-scattering and dose-sensitive 2D or biological materials, where conventional modes have low signal-to-noise or require too much dose. With infinite dose and enough iteration cycles, ptychography has an ideal contrast transfer function [3], but at low dose conditions, iterative ptychography struggles to recover low spatial frequency information. For true low-dose, or less computationally expensive, measurements, the exact thickness of a constant substrate is largely beyond the capabilities of iterative ptychography. In fact, ptychography and other STEM phase contrast techniques like differential phase contrast will largely fail to distinguish bulk substrate from vacuum, as both are low-spatial-frequency objects in the blind spot of these techniques.
